listings.name: Moon River Brewing Company (former City Hotel)
listings.summary: A legislator was shot in the bar of Savannah's City Hotel in 1832, which is documented; tying that to the hauntings is local lore. The 1821 hotel, the city's first, became a brewpub that closed in June 2024.
listings.loreTeaser: The first hotel in Savannah, a bar-room shooting in 1832, a brewery that closed in 2024, and a basement the Ghost Brothers called a portal.

listings.name: The Allen House (Monticello)
listings.summary: A daughter's cyanide poisoning in the late 1940s is the root of a long-running Arkansas ghost legend about this mansion. Built c.1905-06 in Queen Anne and Gothic style for a local businessman.
listings.loreTeaser: A bedroom sealed for decades, a bottle of cyanide on a closet shelf, and a famous Arkansas haunted house.

listings.name: Magnolia Hotel (Seguin)
listings.summary: Local accounts tie this Seguin hotel's haunting to the 1874 ax murder of 12-year-old Emma Voelcker in New Braunfels, whose accused killer reportedly lodged here. It began as an 1840 log cabin and was taking guests by 1844; now a B&B.
listings.loreTeaser: One of Texas's oldest hostelries, once on a most-endangered list, and the inn tied to an 1874 murder case.

listings.name: Old Charleston Jail (Old City Jail)
listings.summary: County jail 1802-1939 that held Denmark Vesey, Union prisoners, pirates, and John and Lavinia Fisher, convicted of robbery and murder and hanged in 1820. The later 'serial killer' legend is disputed.
listings.loreTeaser: A four-story jail with an octagonal tower, a hanging-era roster, and the Fishers, whose legend outgrew the record.

listings.name: Cocke County Memorial Building
listings.summary: After the July 1964 airliner crash near Parrottsville killed 39, this Newport armory served as a temporary morgue, the basis of its haunted reputation. A 1930s armory and American Legion hall, NRHP-listed.
listings.loreTeaser: A 1931 Colonial Revival hall that became a morgue for a night no one in Cocke County forgot.

images.author: Dwight Burdette

listings.name: Beauregard Parish Jail (the Gothic or Hanging Jail)
listings.summary: Joe Genna and Molton Brasseaux were hanged in this DeRidder jail on March 9, 1928, for a 1926 taxi-driver murder, the only hanging in the jail. A 1914 Gothic Revival parish jail, NRHP-listed; tours run.
listings.loreTeaser: A gothic concrete jail with a gallows still on the third floor and one hanging in its history.

listings.address: 220 N Prison Hill Rd, Yuma, AZ 85364
listings.summary: A university study of burial records counts 3,069 inmates, 111 deaths and 104 graves at Arizona Territory's prison, which ran 1876-1909. Now an Arizona State Parks museum.
listings.loreTeaser: Thirty-three years of a desert prison on the Colorado River, and the 'Hell Hole' reputation that still draws visitors.

listings.name: Roff family home (Watseka Wonder)
listings.summary: 1868 Italianate house tied to the 1877-78 'Watseka Wonder' case, in which a teenager was reported to be possessed by a neighbor's daughter who died in 1865. Covered in newspapers of the time.
listings.loreTeaser: One of America's best-documented 19th-century possession cases, played out in two homes in a small Illinois town.

listings.name: Ohio State Reformatory (Mansfield Reformatory)
listings.summary: Documented deaths at this prison include the warden's wife in a 1950 accidental shooting in the family quarters and an officer killed by inmates in 1932. Begun in 1886 and now a tour site; the Shawshank Redemption location.
listings.loreTeaser: A Romanesque prison castle, a cemetery on the grounds, and a long record of tragedy at the warden's quarters.

listings.name: Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum (Weston State Hospital)
listings.summary: A 1935 patient-set fire and numerous patient lobotomies in 1952-55 are part of this Kirkbride asylum's record. Open 1864-1994, built for 250 patients and holding over 2,300 by the 1950s; National Historic Landmark, now a privately owned…
listings.loreTeaser: One of the largest hand-cut stone buildings in North America, built for 250 patients and later packed with thousands.

listings.name: Waverly Hills Sanatorium
listings.summary: Louisville had one of the nation's highest TB death rates when this tuberculosis sanatorium opened in 1910. A 5-story building replaced it in 1926 and the hospital closed in June 1961 as antibiotics cut demand. Tours today.
listings.loreTeaser: A hilltop TB hospital in a city with one of the nation's highest TB death rates, now a tour site that markets its ghosts.

listings.address: 525 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA 95128
listings.place: San Jose, Santa Clara County, CA
listings.summary: 160-room Victorian mansion built nonstop 1884-1922 by Sarah Winchester after the deaths of her infant daughter (1866) and husband (1881). The story that spirits drove the building is legend.
listings.loreTeaser: Stairs to nowhere, 160 rooms, and a widow whose reasons are still argued about.

listings.name: USS Lexington (CV-16) museum ship
listings.address: 2914 N Shoreline Blvd, Corpus Christi, TX 78402
listings.summary: A Japanese torpedo hit on 4 Dec 1943 killed nine crew aboard this Essex-class carrier, and a kamikaze crash in Nov 1944 wrecked her island. Commissioned 1943; now a National Historic Landmark museum ship at Corpus Christi.
listings.loreTeaser: 'The Blue Ghost', the oldest fleet carrier still afloat, with a combat record the ghost stories grow from.

listings.name: Palace Hotel
listings.summary: The 1889 Tibbals Building in Port Townsend ran as a brothel nicknamed the 'Palace of Sweets' from 1925 to 1933, until a sheriff's raid. Restored 1976-88 and run as a hotel; guests report ghosts.
listings.loreTeaser: An 1889 waterfront building with a Prohibition-era brothel past, a sheriff's raid, and guests who report a woman in blue.

listings.name: McRaven House (Bobb House)
listings.summary: Owner John Bobb was shot dead by Union soldiers at what became McRaven, the Bobb House, on 18 May 1864; the National Register record calls him the first Vicksburg civilian killed amid tensions with the occupying Union forces. Now a…
listings.loreTeaser: A siege-battered Vicksburg house where the owner's last quarrel with occupying soldiers ended in gunfire in 1864.

images.caption: McRaven House

listings.name: Lizzie Borden House
listings.summary: 1845 Greek Revival house where Andrew and Abby Borden were killed on 4 August 1892. Lizzie Borden was tried and acquitted in 1893 and no one else was charged. Now a bed and breakfast and museum.
listings.loreTeaser: The 1892 hatchet murders, a trial of the century, and an acquittal that left the case unsolved. Rooms and tours today.

listings.name: Camp Creek Train Wreck Memorial
listings.summary: Public memorial marker in McDonough for the 23 June 1900 Camp Creek train wreck, where a Southern Railway train plunged off a washed-out trestle in a storm and burned. The city's marker counts 39 dead; other accounts say 35.
listings.loreTeaser: Georgia's worst train wreck: a storm, a washed-out trestle, a burning train, and a memorial on Atlanta Street.

listings.name: Old Idaho Penitentiary
listings.summary: The Idaho State Historical Society counts ten executions and about 129 recorded deaths at this Boise prison, which held inmates from 1872 to 1973 and is now a state historic site.
listings.loreTeaser: A sandstone prison with a Rose Garden execution ground, an indoor gallows used once, and about 129 recorded deaths.

listings.name: Wyoming Frontier Prison (old Wyoming State Penitentiary)
listings.summary: WyoHistory.org says 250 people died at this Rawlins penitentiary and 14 men were executed there, nine by hanging and five in the gas chamber. Opened 1901 and closed 1981; now the Wyoming Frontier Prison museum.
listings.loreTeaser: An 80-year prison on the high plains: 14 executions, a gas chamber added in 1936, and a 1912 uprising.

listings.name: Hangman's Building, Virginia City
listings.address: West Wallace Street, Virginia City, MT
listings.summary: On 14 January 1864 Alder Gulch vigilantes hanged five accused road agents from the center roof truss of this Virginia City building while it was under construction. Now a museum run by the Virginia City Preservation Alliance.
listings.loreTeaser: A frontier gold town, a half-built shop, and a beam where vigilantes hanged five men in one day.

images.caption: Hangmans building Virginia City, Montana

listings.name: Houghton Mansion
listings.summary: 1890s home of North Adams' first mayor, Albert C. Houghton. After a 1914 car crash killed his daughter Mary and her friend, Houghton died days later and the chauffeur shot himself in the barn. Later a Masonic lodge; vacant since 2017.
listings.loreTeaser: A mayor's mansion where one road accident claimed four lives in under two weeks.

images.credit: Josh karpf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Houghton Mansion

listings.name: West Virginia Penitentiary
listings.summary: Gothic state prison that held inmates from 1866 to 1995. 94 men were executed there between 1899 and 1959 (85 hanged, nine electrocuted), and inmates took hostages in the 1986 New Year's Day riot. Now a tour site.
listings.loreTeaser: A castle-walled prison with an execution count close to a hundred.

listings.name: Riddle House (Yesteryear Village)
listings.address: Royal Palm Beach area (South Florida Fairgrounds), Palm Beach County, FL
listings.place: Royal Palm Beach area (South Florida Fairgrounds), Palm Beach County, FL
listings.summary: 1905 'Gatekeeper's Cottage' built beside Woodlawn Cemetery in West Palm Beach; it served as a funeral parlor and cemetery keeper's home, later Karl Riddle's residence. Moved to Yesteryear Village in 1995; long told as haunted.
listings.loreTeaser: A cemetery gatekeeper's cottage and funeral parlor, taken apart and rebuilt with its ghost stories intact.

listings.name: Sloss Furnaces National Historic Landmark
listings.summary: Blast furnace that made pig iron from 1882 to 1971, now a free museum. Its company leased convicts to work its mines, including Coalburg, where 90 of 1,000 prisoners died in 1890. Long reported as haunted by workers.
listings.loreTeaser: An iron furnace built on cheap and convict labor, now a museum with a ghost reputation.

listings.name: Preston Castle (Preston School of Industry)
listings.summary: Romanesque reform school opened 1894 and vacated 1960. In 1950 head housekeeper Anna Corbin was found beaten and strangled in the basement; a ward was charged but acquitted and the killing is unsolved. Now run by a foundation for tours.
listings.loreTeaser: A castle for wayward boys with an unsolved 1950 murder in its basement.

listings.address: 1 South Castillo Drive, St. Augustine, FL 32084
listings.place: St. Augustine, St. Johns County, FL
listings.summary: 17th-century Spanish stone fort, later Fort Marion. It held Revolutionary War prisoners and, in 1837, captured Seminole leaders; Uchee Billy died there that November. Now a National Park Service site.
listings.loreTeaser: America's oldest masonry fort, where captured Seminole leaders were held and one died.

listings.name: La Purísima Mission State Historic Park
listings.summary: Spanish mission founded 1787. Smallpox and measles killed several hundred Chumash in 1804-07; the 1812 earthquake destroyed it; in 1824 Chumash revolted and held it until soldiers retook it. Rebuilt as a state park.
listings.loreTeaser: A mission marked by epidemic, earthquake and a Chumash uprising.

listings.loreTeaser: The prison that invented the penitentiary through enforced solitude.

listings.name: Linda Vista Community Hospital (now Hollenbeck Terrace)
listings.address: Boyle Heights, Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, CA
listings.place: Boyle Heights, Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, CA
listings.summary: Santa Fe railroad hospital (1905; 1938 building) that became Linda Vista Community Hospital. Declining care drew criticism before it closed in 1991; it sat empty as a filming set, then became senior housing in 2015.
listings.loreTeaser: A railroad hospital that closed under criticism and became Hollywood's go-to haunted ward.

listings.place: Long Island Sound, off Sands Point (Nassau County) / New Rochelle (Westchester County), NY
listings.summary: 1849-50 granite lighthouse on a rock in Long Island Sound. It survived a 1918 fire and a shipwreck; serial killer Carl Panzram later claimed he dumped victims' bodies near it, and the name carries a drowning legend.
listings.loreTeaser: A lighthouse with an executioner's name, a killer's confession and a legend nobody can prove.

listings.loreTeaser: Where the losers of the O.K. Corral were buried with their boots on.

listings.loreTeaser: One of the most intact 19th-century plantation complexes in the U.S., and the setting for the Ghost Brothers' first episode.

listings.address: Middletown area (Madison Township), Butler County, OH
listings.place: Middletown area (Madison Township), Butler County, OH
listings.summary: Former 1937-2000 elementary school in the Poasttown area; nearby train wrecks in 1895 and 1910 (24 killed in 1910, per Middletown Historical Society records) feed its haunted reputation.
listings.loreTeaser: A closed rural school whose haunted reputation is tied to two Fourth of July train wrecks a mile away.

listings.name: House of Wills (former funeral home)
listings.summary: 1899 hall that housed Ohio's largest Black funeral home (J. W. Wills Co.) from 1941 to 2005; NRHP-listed. Vacant for years; reportedly sold by the city c.2011-12. Episode's 'built to trap energy' claim is unverified.
listings.loreTeaser: A pink-painted funeral home that served Cleveland's Black community for six decades before it went dark.

listings.name: Thornhaven Manor
listings.summary: Farmhouse reported built c.1845, featured on 'Ghost Adventures' in 2013. Lore links it to a 1906 poisoning; whether that happened at this house is disputed. Not occupied by its owner.
listings.loreTeaser: An 1840s Indiana farmhouse with a poisoning story that may belong to the house down the road.

media.title: Thornhaven Manor & Magnolia Plantation: Ghostin' Edition

listings.name: Vulture Mine and Vulture City
listings.summary: Arizona's most productive gold mine (1863-1942) and its abandoned town, now a privately owned tour site. The 'hanging tree' tale of ore thieves is legend; historians cited by a 2016 report found no records.
listings.loreTeaser: A gold-rush boom town, a famous ironwood tree, and a legend that is better than the record.

listings.name: The 'Conjuring House' farmhouse (Burrillville)
listings.summary: Early farmhouse in Burrillville made famous by The Conjuring and a family's 1970s haunting account. Local historians say the 'witch' story attached to it has no records behind it.
listings.loreTeaser: A real farmhouse, a famous film, and a local woman wrongly cast as its witch.

listings.name: Tampa Theatre
listings.summary: 1926 atmospheric movie palace by John Eberson, NRHP-listed and still a working non-profit cinema. Staff tell of longtime projectionist Foster 'Fink' Finley (1930-65) still 'coming to work'.
listings.loreTeaser: A 1926 movie palace and a projectionist who, the staff say, never clocked out.

listings.name: David Stewart Farm
listings.summary: Farm west of Gettysburg used as a Confederate field hospital in July-August 1863, marked by a 1983 state historical marker. Privately owned; the family's own ghost accounts are the haunting lore.
listings.loreTeaser: A battle-summer field hospital on a farm that is still lived on today.

listings.name: Wright Square
listings.summary: 1733-plan city square tied by ghost tours to Alice Riley, the servant hanged in 1735 for killing her master. Records confirm the hanging but not the square as the site; the square holds Tomochichi's burial.
listings.loreTeaser: Savannah's 'hanging square' and the servant who may never have hanged there.

listings.name: Ash Street Jail
listings.summary: Bristol County jail built in 1888 and still operating; Lizzie Borden was held there for the 12 days of her 1893 trial. It is an active jail and cannot be visited.
listings.loreTeaser: Where Lizzie Borden spent her trial, inside a jail that never closed.

listings.name: Emlen Physick Estate
listings.place: Cape May, Cape May County, NJ
listings.summary: 1879 Frank Furness mansion built for Dr. Emlen Physick Jr., his mother and Aunt Emilie; saved from demolition in 1970 and run as a house museum. Local lore says the Physick family still lingers.
listings.loreTeaser: Cape May's 'original haunted house,' where local lore says the last of the Physicks never fully left.

listings.name: Michigan's First State Prison (Armory Arts Village)
listings.summary: Michigan's first state prison opened here in 1839. An 1875 legislative investigation documented harsh punishments, including the lash and the cross, and a 1912 riot brought the National Guard inside the walls. It closed in 1934.
listings.loreTeaser: The original Jackson walled prison, later an armory, is now an arts village with guided historic prison tours.

listings.name: Jackson Poor Farm Cemetery (former Jackson County Poor Farm)
listings.summary: A fire on January 24, 1886, destroyed the Jackson County poorhouse and killed five residents, according to the 2023 state historical marker. The farm closed in 1963; a 1967 fire left only this cemetery of unmarked graves.
listings.loreTeaser: A fenced roadside cemetery of unmarked graves is all that remains of the county poor farm, where five residents died in an 1886 fire.

listings.name: Otsego Hotel (Otsego Apartments)
listings.summary: The northwest corner of this hotel collapsed during construction on October 11, 1902, killing a Grass Lake worker and injuring four. Rebuilt and opened in 1904, it was a leading downtown hotel until 1962 and later became senior housing.
listings.loreTeaser: A railroad-era hotel that partly collapsed during construction, was rebuilt, and still stands at Michigan and Francis. Senior housing; view from the sidewalk.

listings.name: State Prison of Southern Michigan (the Walls)
listings.summary: In April 1952, about 200 inmates at the State Prison of Southern Michigan rioted and held nine guards hostage for five days, causing millions of dollars in damage. The old walled prison is closed; active state prisons still operate nearby.
listings.loreTeaser: The later Jackson walled prison, once among the world's largest, was the scene of a five-day hostage mutiny in 1952.

listings.name: Michigan Central Railroad Jackson Depot (Union Station)
listings.summary: On October 13, 1893, a World's Fair excursion train ran into the rear of another train standing at Jackson's Michigan Central depot. The 1873 union station still serves passengers today.
listings.loreTeaser: The 1873 Michigan Central station, still in passenger use, was the scene of a deadly 1893 World's Fair crash. View it from East Michigan; stay off the tracks.

listings.name: Jackson Junction rail crash site (1879)
listings.address: Elm Avenue railroad crossing, Jackson, MI 49201
listings.summary: On October 10, 1879, a westbound Michigan Central express collided with a freight engine at Jackson Junction, just east of the Elm Avenue crossing. It remains one of the city's deadliest railroad wrecks.
listings.loreTeaser: The 1879 wreck happened at Jackson Junction, just east of the Elm Avenue crossing. View from the public street only; do not enter the railroad right-of-way.

listings.name: Dixboro ghost (Oak Grove Cemetery)
listings.summary: Local legend says the ghost of Martha Mulholland, called the Dixboro ghost, appeared in the mid-1840s to a man lodging in her former house and told of her murder. The house is long gone; a cemetery marker in Dixboro still tells the tale.
listings.loreTeaser: A Dixboro legend of a ghost who said she had been murdered, remembered on the cemetery marker. The vanished house was a private home and is not mapped here.

listings.name: County Farm Park (former Washtenaw County poorhouse)
listings.summary: The public park on Platt Road occupies the former Washtenaw County poorhouse grounds, bought in 1836. A brick county infirmary later stood at the Washtenaw Avenue end of the grounds; it closed in 1971 and was torn down in 1979.
listings.loreTeaser: The old county poor farm is now Nelson Meade County Farm Park, open public land on Platt Road. The poorhouse and infirmary buildings are gone.

listings.name: Washtenaw County jail site (North Main Street)
listings.address: 625 North Main Street, Ann Arbor, MI 48104
listings.summary: The county jail on this North Main Street site held prisoners from the late 1830s until 1887. After a murder conviction, Charles Chorr was sentenced to hang, then escaped and was never recaptured. A community center occupies the site today.
listings.loreTeaser: The early county jail stood here on North Main, where a condemned prisoner escaped after his death sentence. A community center stands on the site.

listings.name: National House Inn
listings.summary: Andrew Mann built this inn in 1835, and it is reported to be the first brick building in Calhoun County. It later served as a wagon and windmill factory before being restored as an inn. Local folklore tells of a Lady in Red in its halls.
listings.loreTeaser: Local legend says a woman in a red dress drifts through the halls of this 1835 stagecoach inn. The longtime manager says she has never seen her.

listings.name: Crying Mary statue (Oak Hill Cemetery)
listings.summary: A bronze figure of Memory stands over Johannes Decker's grave in Oak Hill Cemetery, commissioned by his widow in 1911. Local legend calls her Crying Mary and says she weeps after dark; rain streaks in the patina likely started the tale.
listings.loreTeaser: Legend says the statue weeps for a terrible crime. The truth is a widow's grief and a century of rain. Visit during cemetery hours.

listings.name: Camp Custer (1918 influenza epidemic)
listings.address: Fort Custer Industrial Park, Battle Creek, MI
listings.place: Battle Creek (Fort Custer), Calhoun County, MI
listings.summary: Camp Custer was built here in 1917 to train World War I soldiers. Influenza reached the camp on September 29, 1918, and in about four weeks more than 600 soldiers died. The site later became Fort Custer.
listings.loreTeaser: In the fall of 1918 the flu filled the camp hospital, then the mess halls and barracks, with the sick and dying.

listings.name: Tasty Cafe bombing site (1967)
listings.summary: On August 18, 1967, a mailed package marked as books exploded inside the Tasty Cafe on Michigan Avenue, killing one of the cafe's owners as she opened it. A conviction won in 1970 was overturned in 1975 over a 27-month trial delay.
listings.loreTeaser: A parcel marked 'books' came in with the morning mail to a Main Street diner. Marshall has never forgotten what happened next.

listings.name: Calhoun County Poor Farm Cemetery
listings.address: Foxcroft Drive near 18 1/2 Mile Road, Marshall, MI 49068 (USGS cemetery point)
listings.summary: In December 1849 Calhoun County bought farmland northeast of Marshall for a poor farm, which opened in September 1850 with seventeen residents. The poor, the insane and neglected children lived there; its cemetery is recorded here.
listings.loreTeaser: From 1850 the county sent its poor, aged and insane to a farm outside Marshall. A federal cemetery record still marks the spot. View from the road only.

listings.name: Abandoned house west of Homer
listings.summary: An abandoned house stands in rural Clarendon Township, west of Homer. No published history for the property has been found yet.
listings.loreTeaser: An abandoned house west of Homer. Its story is still unwritten.
listings.geo_source: Neighborhood circle (offset center, not the house; Archive privacy rule)

listings.name: Crouch farm (1883 murders)
listings.address: Spring Arbor Township, Jackson County, MI
listings.place: Spring Arbor Township, Jackson County, MI
listings.summary: Four people were shot to death in their beds at a Spring Arbor Township farmhouse on November 22, 1883: Jacob Crouch, his pregnant daughter Eunice White, her husband Henry White, and visitor Moses Polley. No one was convicted.
listings.loreTeaser: Jackson County's most infamous unsolved murders, later wrapped in a cemetery legend that the victims still meet.
listings.geo_source: Neighborhood circle (offset center, not the house; Archive privacy rule)
listings.area: eastern Spring Arbor Township, northeast of Horton

listings.name: Mary Latimer murder (Jackson)
listings.summary: In January 1889, Mary Latimer was found shot to death in her Jackson home. Her son, Robert Irving Latimer, was convicted of the murder and sentenced to life in the state prison.
listings.loreTeaser: A notorious 1889 Jackson matricide that ended in a life sentence at the old state prison. Private homes nearby; view from the street only.
listings.geo_source: Neighborhood circle (offset center, not the house; Archive privacy rule)
listings.area: west side of Jackson, south of West Michigan Avenue

listings.name: Deborah Greene murder (Liberty Township)
listings.summary: On January 22, 1878, Deborah Green, an aged widow, was murdered in her home in Liberty Township. An inquest blamed a person or persons unknown. A man was later tried, but the jury could not agree and the case was dropped.
listings.loreTeaser: An unsolved 1878 murder somewhere in Liberty Township. The house site is unknown, so the whole township is shown. Private land; view from public roads only.
listings.geo_source: Whole-township area (center is not the site; Archive privacy rule)
listings.area: Liberty Township (whole township; exact site unknown)
